title: incident-bot: add oncall runbook quicklinks + fallback for private runbooks
author: Asha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: On-call engineers frequently need to open runbooks from alerts. The incident-bot previously posted runbook titles and SLO links but did not provide one-click quicklinks when runbooks live behind private URLs or require alternate access paths. This PR adds a runbook quicklinks UI element and a fallback behavior that surface private-runbook access instructions when direct links are blocked.

What this changes: - Adds quicklinks rendering for runbook entries in the oncall notification card. Quicklinks are resolved from runbook metadata; when a public URL is available we render a one-click link. If a runbook is marked private we render an inline "Access instructions" modal with team-specific steps and a link to request access. - Adds a small cache to avoid repeated lookups for popular runbooks in a short window. Cache respects TTL and invalidation hooks. - Adds telemetry for quicklink clicks, access-fallback impressions, and request-access flows (incident_bot.runbook.quicklink.click, .fallback_shown, .access_request.initiated). - Adds unit + integration tests and an end-to-end smoke test in staging.

Implementation notes: - incident-bot/src/handlers/runbook_quicklinks.py: new resolver and renderer. - incident-bot/web/components/Quicklinks.tsx: UI component with graceful degradation for private links. - incident-bot/tests/test_quicklinks.py: coverage for public/private branches and cache behavior. - docs/oncall/runbooks.md: docs section describing quicklinks and access request flow.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation completed - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration smoke test in staging - [x] Docs updated - [x] Product reviewed (ENG/Oncall)

Rollout: feature gated under incident_bot.quicklinks flag. Will enable for 25% of alerts initially and monitor quicklink click-through and access-request rate for 72h before full rollout.
